claims.text: Greg Short asserts that courage is not the absence of fear but action taken in the presence of fear: a brave person feels fear and acts anyway, while a coward feels fear and does not act because of it. The distinction is behavioral, not emotional — the feeling of fear is present in both cases; only the response differs.
claims.speaker: Greg Short

claims.text: Greg Short argues that waiting for a perfect environment before confronting fears is a mistake; fears should be engaged immediately regardless of circumstances. Delaying until conditions feel right means the confrontation is perpetually deferred.
claims.speaker: Greg Short

claims.text: Greg Short claims that failing to conquer one's fears produces end-of-life regret independent of business or career success: a person can be successful in business and entrepreneurship yet still reach old age knowing they did not face their fears, and that knowledge is its own form of loss.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Applies across all adults regardless of professional success
bounded_by: Does not mean business success is unachievable for those who avoid fears — only that a separate form of regret accumulates

practices.text: Identify any category of your life where you are behaving like a coward — where fear is causing inaction — and immediately go after that thing.
